title: Book 11 opens: priesthood; legal type of priesthood in Christ
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK ELEVEN. Concerning priesthood, and that according to law it was a type of the one in Christ.

Cyril: Concerning the tent at least and the things oracled upon it, a word sufficient for us very well and gracefully polished unto spiritual thinness has been finished. And it would be fitting, as at least it seems to me—and you yourself also will somehow agree, I know—to take hold of the honors of priesthood, and again in what manner through the one in type and according to law the true is signified—that is, the one in Christ and through him sanctifying the sacred race, and I mean again those who have been flashed in faith, and who have been enriched with intimacy unto God, through at least having shared holy Spirit.
Palladius: For it would be fitting and very reasonably.

Cyril: So then with the holy tent having been completed in fitting beauty, and having been brought into the form shown on the mountain to all-divine Moses, God was making the showing-forth of the priests, and indeed also was saying, ‘And you bring toward yourself both Aaron your brother and his sons from
translator_notes: Ends mid into §2 sons of Israel; PG mid-cut kept.

title: Named call to priesthood; Aaron type of Christ; Moses must draw Aaron near
english: Cyril: …of the sons of Israel to priest for me, Aaron and Nadab and Abihu, and Eleazar, and Ithamar sons of Aaron.’ So then by name the chosen have been called toward sacred-work. ‘For no one takes the honor for himself, but the one being called by God,’ according to what has been written. So then let no one go self-chosen unto priesting for God, but let him wait a call, or if attempting to snatch what he does not have by the votes from above, he will undergo the justice of Dathan and Abiram. And do not marvel if the self-chosen among us is outlandish and unbeautiful, when also concerning Christ himself Paul writes, ‘He did not glorify himself to become high priest, but the one who spoke toward him, You are a priest unto the age according to the order of Melchizedek.’ So then of the call the one said upon Christ an image again would be the wisely said toward Moses, ‘And you bring toward yourself both Aaron your brother, and his sons.’ For the, Bring toward, what else makes clear except the, Make intimate and call toward? And Christ has been called as unto high priest through counsel of the Father. And somehow with him also the all-divine disciples have been called-together and set as fellow-workers toward sacred-work. Therefore also they were saying expressly, ‘For we are fellow-workers of God’; and they were going around again all the under-sun, sacred-working unto the nations the Gospel of Christ. For they have been called unto apostleship through Christ, and true is the word. But the matter was somehow altogether also willed by the Father; for one upon all the things done is the vote, because also counsel and wisdom and will of the Father is the Son. So then Aaron would be a type of Christ, and of the priesthood thought in spirit and truth, as it were a pre-showing-forth, as still in the dimmer shadows. And understand that Moses is ordered to bring toward himself Aaron; for somehow weak and incomplete is the law, even if it should be put apart from Christ. ‘For impossible for blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.’ And Christ having brought forward one sacrifice for sinners has perfected unto the continual those being sanctified. So then let those still friends of shadow and letter, and deemed worthy of Mosaic commands, know that unless they should bring toward themselves the high priest and apostle of our confession Jesus the Christ, unto nothing for them will the zeal of the worship in type finish. For what boasts would there be beside the virtue-loving God of the life in law? Therefore also all-wise Paul for us, through the surpassing of the knowledge of Christ, says to think dung the things in world, and to choose instead the spiritual things; and this is intelligibly the bringing toward himself Aaron himself.
Palladius: I understand what you say; for clear is the word.
Cyril: Bring toward yourself then, he says,

title: Aaron helps weak Moses; priestly garments = put on Christ
english: Cyril: …Aaron your brother, and according to another manner, I think, knowing the matter not unhelpful unto benefit as in spiritual thinking; and understand what I say. For Moses was being sent, leading Israel out from the misery in Egypt. Then seeing the attempt standing far beyond human power, and beyond measures of the strength and eloquence present for him, he was entreating saying: ‘Behold I am not well-spoken before yesterday, nor before the third, nor from when you began to speak to your attendant; thin-voiced and slow-tongued am I.’ And with God toward these saying, ‘Who gave a mouth to a human? who made hard-of-hearing and deaf, seeing and blind? Did not I Lord God? And now go, and I will open your mouth.’ Being worsted by the superiority of the achievements he was fearing again, and indeed was saying, ‘I beg, Lord, appoint another, the one able, whom you will send.’ And God was appointing at that time at once Aaron, unto a type of Christ who knows how to set upright all things easily; and Israel has been ransomed not otherwise, unless as a fellow-worker for Moses’ thin-speech and weakness again, as in an image in Aaron, Christ has been given; thus also here you will think. For perfecting the weak of the law in Christ, he brought Aaron alongside unto priesthood, and joins him usefully to blessed Moses. For neither unto ransom would the law suffice, nor indeed unto being able to perfect unto sanctification those who have been ransomed. And ransom and sanctification is Christ, with saints working-together; just as indeed Moses with Aaron in Egypt then, and with Aaron himself the sons. And with the high priest and leader of all, Christ, the all-divine disciples were also working-together intelligibly. Not running together as with one weak, though being able to set upright all things, but as having been called toward service and chosen by merit, and gaining from him the well-strong upon all. And all-divine Paul will witness saying: ‘I am strong for all things in the Christ who empowers me.’
Palladius: So then chosen and by name have Aaron and the rest been called toward sacred-liturgy.

Cyril: And in addition to these at least he was legislating bright and priest-fitting garments to be constructed for them saying: ‘And you will make a holy stole for Aaron your brother unto honor and glory, and you speak to all the wise in understanding, whom I have filled with spirit of sense, and they will make the holy stole of Aaron unto the holy, in which he will priest for me.’ So then all-wise Paul advises those justified in faith that the truly holy and from-heaven stole must be put on writing: ‘Put on our Lord Jesus Christ.’ For this indeed the prophet Isaiah has cried beforehand saying as from person of the Church, ‘Let my soul rejoice upon the Lord, for he has put on me a garment of salvation and a tunic of gladness.’ So then a garment the unto

title: Christ the garment of honor; gold/purple/linen/scarlet/hyacinth = Word’s glory
english: Cyril: …honor and glory truly for the sacred and holy race is Christ, a bright and beyond-world adornment for the souls of the saints. ‘For as many as into Christ you were baptized, Christ you put on,’ he says, and true is the word. And as in shadows the law beautifies Aaron, carrying up unto Christ the glory from having been dressed many-formedly. For all but also woven-together with the construction of the craft-works a mystical and exact word is found, showing riddlingly the glory of the Savior. For see how he says the craftsmen of the garments have been filled with the understanding from God, carrying them unto flower-bright embroidery, and writing the glory of Christ into the robes. And breastpiece and shoulder-piece, and foot-reaching robe, and the tasseled tunic, and headdress and belt, the things being crafted, these and in addition to them others, which also part by part for us, as possible, will be said. So then he said concerning those taken into the works, ‘And they will take the gold, and the hyacinth, and the purple, and the scarlet, and linen.’ And again casting a thin mind into the things set forth for me, and before at least the others observe this.
Palladius: What sort of thing do you say?
Cyril: For have not of gold and linen, and indeed also purple and spun scarlet, and hyacinth again all the things in the tent been made, and it was unto a type of Christ?
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: And see that through the same also the stole of the one excelling in priesthood has been arranged, travailing the glory of Christ as again in an image and types; for the same words, and not another knowledge, signify the beauty of Christ. For he is known as in gold God, as in purple having the kingly dignity, and as in fine linen a thin and bodiless word, as in scarlet through the flesh; and in air-appearing hyacinth—for such-colored is hyacinth—through the from-above and from heaven. Or is not the Word from God Father both God together and king?
Palladius: How not?
Cyril: And being Word of the Father thin and bodiless, has he not come to be in flesh and is he from above?
Palladius: True.

Cyril: So then the same materials indistinguishably and as in thin contemplation both of the garments, and indeed also of the things constructed in the holy tent. And these things thus; and the things unto honor and glory for Aaron many-formedly woven it is already time to say. So then, ‘And they will make,’ he says, ‘the shoulder-piece from spun linen, a woven work of an embroiderer, two shoulder-pieces holding together will be for him, one the other upon the two parts having been hung. And the weave of the

title: Ephod emerald stones = Israel on Christ’s shoulders; heaven-colored memorial
english: Cyril: …shoulder-pieces, which is upon it according to the making, from it will be from gold and hyacinth and purple and scarlet spun-through and spun linen.’ And having given the material already said beforehand to the weaves, at once he adds: ‘And you will take the two stones, emerald stones, and you will engrave in them the names of the sons of Israel, six names about the one stone, and the six remaining names upon the second stone, according to their births, a work of stone-working craft; an engraving of a seal you will engrave the stones upon the names of the sons of Israel. And you will set the two stones upon the shoulders of the shoulder-piece; stones of memorial are they for the sons of Israel.’
Palladius: Deep, as it seems, is the word in the contemplations; and try first to say that, what is the matter of the so-called shoulder-piece, or what manner of construction it would have.

Cyril: He has ordered some weave as in form of a tunic and reaching as far as the chest to come to be, as having been brought upon the garments themselves inward and as on skin and as far as feet, and flashing the ray from gold and purple, it would birth for the eyes of those watching a solemn and priest-fitting marvel. This he has called shoulder-piece, through, I think, the short of the craft-work, and the barely stretching upon both shoulders. So then in this shoulder-piece two stones—and these of emerald—well bound with thin threads he was clearly typing must be fixed, with the tribes having been dug-in artfully by name, so that six be written in one stone. And what is the word of this, he himself was clarifying for us saying: ‘And Aaron will take the names of the sons of Israel opposite Lord upon his two shoulders, a memorial concerning them.’
Palladius: And what again through the stones and the things in them will we think to be hinted?

Cyril: Hear then; pale is the emerald stone. And the ray-formed is swimming in it in depth, and as it were light has been mixed with dark; each dragging the conquering toward itself. So then, O Palladius, looking toward the high and above, the eye of the body, and straining unto the deep toward aether and heaven, will it not cast forward some such contemplation? for pale somehow and as in depth black, and mixed with moderate light, is the uppermost aether.
Palladius: Thus it holds.

Cyril: So then an image of heaven the sacred Letter makes the stone. And do not marvel when also with sapphire it likens it again. For pale is the sapphire, and not far from the sight in emerald. And it has been written thus in the Exodus, ‘And Moses and Aaron went up, and Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the eldership of Israel. And they saw the place where the God of Israel had stood; and the things under his feet, as a work of sapphire stone, and as form of firmament of the heaven, in the cleanness.’
translator_notes: Ends at Exod 24 quote; Egypt idolatry continues §6.

title: Heaven under God’s feet; names in heaven on Christ; breastpiece of judgments begins
english: Cyril: For since having come to be in Egypt those from Israel have served the creation, and were calling heaven god, usefully the Lord of the wholes was also appearing having stepped upon the firmament itself, that they might know that he has all things under feet, and is master of the heavens themselves, as craftsman. So then you understand that as some type and imaging of heaven the sacred Letter makes the stone pale-ing as in moderate light? for blue-rayed by nature.
Palladius: You have spoken most excellently.

Cyril: So then a sign of heaven is the emerald, having Israel written according to race, and having obtained as place the shoulder-piece, through which it will be present to think, that whoever should be those who have obtained the registration in heaven, these altogether and wholly will rest upon Christ, all but also having them upon shoulders, and making the good as in an order of children. And such also the divine Moses said, beautifying Israel with the sparing from God: ‘As an eagle should shelter its nest, and upon its nestlings it yearned, spreading its wings it received them, and took them up upon its mid-backs.’ But somehow also David sings for every holy one, and one having dwelt in help of the Highest, ‘Upon his mid-backs he will overshadow you,’ he says. Mid-backs somehow as I myself think the under-neck parts, and the as in shoulders hinting, and not altogether the backs. So then upon shoulders they will be lifted, according to the prophet’s voice, and upon arm they will be taken up according to the ancient Ephraim, those who have obtained the above registration, which as well-famed and worthy-of-marvel and lying-above the beauty of the divine gifts the Savior himself has declared, saying thus to the holy disciples: ‘Do not rejoice that the demons are subjected to you, but rejoice rather that your names have been written in the heavens.’ And he says the registration at least in the stones will be a memorial for the sons of Israel opposite Lord, all but also of one gazing-intently, as in Aaron; for God and Father receives us unto remembrance in Christ, and we have become in him both known and worthy of oversight, and as in a book of God.
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly.

Cyril: And another adornment he orders must be brought alongside for this saying, ‘And you will make little shields from pure gold having been mixed, and you will make two tassels from pure gold having been mixed in flowers a work of plaiting, and you will set the plaited tassels upon the little shields and their shoulder-straps from the front things. And you will make an oracle of the judgments, a work of a weaver according to the rhythm of the shoulder-piece, you will make it from gold and hyacinth, and purple and spun scarlet, and spun linen, you will make it square, it will be double of a span the length and of a span the breadth, And you will weave in it a weave according to the
notes_covered: Egypt served creation; God above firmament

title: Twelve breastpiece stones; construction of oracle; why ‘oracle of judgments’
english: Cyril: …four-rowed stone.’ Then having composed the names of the stones, he adds again, ‘And the stones will be from the names of the sons of Israel twelve, according to their names, engravings of seals of each according to their names will be unto the twelve tribes.’ And next after a few: ‘And Aaron will take,’ he says, ‘the names of the sons of Israel upon the oracle of the judgment, upon the chest when entering into the Holy, a memorial opposite Lord God.’
Palladius: How deep the matter of the oracle, and altogether hard-to-reach even the manner of the construction seems to me to be.

Cyril: So then one must go upon them, and as very near the truth, even if the steepness does not perhaps allow to reach it altogether. For to see the very unclear things even at least in a mirror, I myself would say differs from the other—I mean from not having been thought at all. So then I will say, as possible and as I would have according to mind. He has ordered two little shields to come to be from pure gold, broader than according to a circle of a coin, yet in the same form; for circular is the coin; then two tassels mixed in flowers from pure gold. And we say the tassels are chains, having the sight as in colors having been varied. For he said flowers the colors. And linen then was also purple these, and a golden thread, and indeed also hyacinth, and the scarlet twist. And in addition to this at least he says a square weave must come to be, and as in form of a cube, span-measured, equal-sided everywhere. And he says the twelve stones must be woven in it very well, and lying three each, as in four whole rows with the tribes having been carved in them by name. So then from the shoulder-piece, the little shields having been hung with golden and many-formed chains were sitting under gently, seeming both high and to be upon the shoulders themselves. And they were touching the chests and already were hanging upon the breasts themselves; and from at least the little shields with other chains the oracle of the judgments well fastened was floating upon the chest, with tassels having been hung. And the matter was not unmarvelous for those seeing, translucent with stones and gold and with the good-colors of the other materials having been worked all-gloriously. And this again will be unto remembrance for the sons of Israel, opposite Lord when Aaron enters into the Holy. So then is the shape of the craft-works clear for you as possible now?
Palladius: And very much. And instead of what then the name oracle of the judgments for the craft-work?
Cyril: For have we not also said etymologizing that the upper has been called shoulder-piece, through having been stretched upon both shoulders?
Palladius: Yes. What then is this at least?
Cyril: That again etymologically and proportionally the as

title: Oracle on heart = right judgment; saints as precious stones; arms of righteousness
english: Cyril: …having been set away in heart and inwards we say has been named oracle of the judgments. For as a dwelling of the rational in us is heart and inwards. And as it were has been fixed and naturally planted in the rational in us also the upright and unblamable judgment upon each of the things to be practiced—that is, the righteous-judging, and what is fitting for each; for does not some rational in us weigh the natures of the things to be practiced, and separate from the better the graceless and unbeneficial?
Palladius: And altogether.

Cyril: And custom for the God-breathed Scripture is to name judgment the uprightness and righteous-judging. And indeed all-divine David sings: ‘Blessed those who keep judgment, and who do righteousness in every season.’ And he said somewhere again: ‘And honor of a king is to love judgment.’ For bright is the honor and glory of a king, loving righteousness. So then an oracle of judgment is the having been cast upon heart and chest, through as it were lying in a place of the rational, in which is the uprightness in righteousness. And in this very thing twelve stones held-around with gold, having writing, the tribes. And they would be a type of holy men, who are both bright and honored, and as some choice stones, all but also lying unto mind and heart of Christ; for they are truly worthy of memory, through at least the conspicuous in virtue, and the honored as in sanctification. And from the oracle of the judgments golden tassels also hang, the matter hinting, I think, that of the multitude of the saints the much and unnumbered swarm of achievements is all but also seen having been hung. And indeed blessed David also says the adornment of the Church is in tassels.
Palladius: Persuasive is the word.

Cyril: And from at least the oracle of the judgments a varied and good-colored chain held with golden rings creeps up, just as we were saying, and going through both little shields, reaches unto the very tip of the shoulder-piece, upon which are the stones of the registration. And what this also would be, how is it not worthy to see? So then the riddle seems to me to hint again some such thing: For as the precious stones both in knowledge and in memory of Christ, running toward the above registration, gain the matter through the weapons of righteousness of the right and left; for thus clearly all-divine Paul writes. And indeed also elsewhere he says: ‘Put on the full-armor of God.’ And golden are the king’s weapons, and golden likewise the little shields, and riddlingly showing the full-armor of God. So then we will be not otherwise in memory and registration of God, unless having grasped the weapons of righteousness, and going through them practically. And the having been fastened of the shoulder-piece
notes_covered: saints = precious stones on Christ’s heart

title: Breastpiece joins above/below; twelve stones = faith/firmness; Urim/Thummim = Christ
english: Cyril: …the oracle would signify, I think, the below having been joined to the above, with Christ mediating. ‘For he himself is our peace, the one who has made both one,’ according to the Scriptures, and having fastened the human things to the multitude of the holy angels with the bond of love. And one must know that also blessed Ezekiel says the ruler of Tyre has put on every precious stone; and he counts these, which also all-divine Moses says have been set in the oracle of the judgments. And these were, sardius, topaz, emerald, carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper, ligure, agate, amethyst, chrysolite, beryl, onyx. And they had been arranged three each, and in whole four rows, the such placing sketching for us the firm in faith of those in heart and memory of Christ. For of faith is the three each, and as in Trinity a symbol; and of firmness the as in a square and equal-sided shape. For thus the oracle had been made, upon which also the twelve stones.
Palladius: I am persuaded.

Cyril: And in addition to these at least he orders also something else to be woven-together with the twelve stones, saying: ‘And you will set upon the oracle of the judgment the disclosure and the truth, and it will be upon the chest of Aaron, when he enters into the Holy opposite Lord, and Aaron will bring in the judgments of the sons of Israel upon the chest opposite Lord through all.’ So then he names disclosure and truth, yet he has not still also made clear distinctly whether stones, or as on a small tablet a writing he has ordered to come to be. And I will remember a prophet saying, ‘Because for many days the sons of Israel will sit, there not being a king, nor a ruler, there not being a sacrifice, nor there being an altar, nor a priesthood, nor disclosures.’ But whether these also should be stones, or as on a golden tablet a writing of the names, the word will not investigate very much, and we will know they have been set unto a type, of Christ being present with saints. ‘For behold,’ he says, ‘I am with you all the days, and until completion of the age.’ And truth and disclosure is Christ. For in him we have known the Father, and he has disclosed for us his good will the perfect and well-pleasing, according to the Scriptures. For somewhere Christ said: ‘No longer do I say you slaves, you are my friends, because all things which I heard from my Father I announced to you.’ And truth also otherwise is Emmanuel, because he alone by nature is Son, and as from God God, alone holy, alone Lord; and by participation is the creation, and according to imitation, as many as he himself is thought to be. So then Christ is present with the saints as being thought in disclosure and truth, who also in person of the Father brings in the things according to us, always living unto the interceding for us. For this, I think, is the, And Aaron will bring in the judgments of the sons of Israel
translator_notes: Ends mid into §10 upon chest always.

title: Hyacinth robe = above immortality; pomegranates/bells = Gospel economy entry
english: Cyril: …opposite Lord upon his chest through all.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: And a priest-fitting and worthy-of-marvel garment he orders must be constructed saying: ‘And you will make an under-garment foot-reaching, wholly hyacinth, and the mouth-around will be from it middle, having a hem in a circle of the mouth-around, a work of a weaver, the joining woven-together from it, that it may not be torn. And you will make under the border of the under-garment below, as of a pomegranate flowering pomegranate-lets from hyacinth, and purple, and scarlet spun-through, and spun linen, under the border of the under-garment in a circle. The same form for the pomegranate-lets, and golden bells in midst of these in a circle beside a golden pomegranate-bell, and flowered upon the border of the under-garment in a circle. And Aaron when liturgizing, his voice will be audible, when entering into the Holy opposite Lord, and when going out, that he may not die.’ So then under-garment and foot-reaching, a long tunic, both well-formed toward wrapping-around, and the going from the neck itself unto extreme feet, he names clearly; and from hyacinth, because a symbol of the above immortality—that is, of Christ. For such indeed also all-divine David has announced beforehand saying as from person of God concerning those sacred-working in the churches: ‘Her priests I will put on salvation.’ Put on our Lord Jesus Christ, also wise Paul charges us. And this, I think, is our dwelling the from heaven, which we yearn to put on, the tunic of gladness, the garment of the salvation, according to the prophet’s voice. And a type of heaven is the hyacinth color said clearly. And true is the word, as upon us ourselves. For we have been wrapped with the immortality from above. And if also Christ himself should be thought, as in Aaron having the foot-reaching under-garment, no less true for us is the word; for being God by nature the Only-begotten, he finishes his own body incorruptible, and having wrapped it with the life from above, he was somehow altogether setting it in better things than the greed of death; for that both naturally together and unparticipatedly in Christ are both immortality and life, you will understand also from here. For he said as indeed also existing by nature God, ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’ And being life-made according to the human, ‘For just as the Father,’ he says, ‘has life in himself, so also to the Son he has given to have life in himself.’ So then even if Christ himself should be thought, the one said to have been wrapped with the immortality from above, the word would not go out from the fitting. And in addition at least to the below parts perhaps, pomegranate-lets and bells alternating the things lying in; and pomegranate-lets as woven-together, and golden the bells; that they might be well-sounding according to the true, and indeed also when Aaron runs into the Holies of holies, they make his running-in most notable. And this also is a symbol of the saving and wise economy—I mean of the divine and Gospel
translator_notes: Ends mid κηρύγματος into §11; PG mid-cut kept.
